caption:
"How do you deep copy an object?" If your answer is JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()), expect a follow-up.

Look at the card. JSON.stringify turns a Date into a string, and JSON.parse doesn't turn it back. So copy.placedAt is a string and getTime() throws. The same trip silently drops undefined values and functions, and turns a Map or Set into an empty object.

structuredClone is built into modern browsers and Node 17+. It copies Dates, Maps, Sets and nested objects properly. It throws on functions instead of dropping them quietly.

JSON is still fine for plain data that came from an API.

Source: MDN, structuredClone().
